subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does 'rit.' (ritardando) mean?
questions.explain: Ritardando means to gradually slow the tempo down.

questions.q: Which term refers to the tone quality or 'colour' of a sound that lets you tell a flute from a violin?
questions.explain: Timbre, or sonority, is the characteristic tone colour that distinguishes one instrument or voice from another.

questions.q: A texture in which all parts share the melody but decorate it differently at the same time is called:
questions.explain: Heterophonic texture has performers playing variations of the same melody simultaneously.

questions.q: Compared with a major scale, a (natural) minor key generally sounds:
questions.explain: Minor keys typically sound darker or sadder than the brighter major.

questions.q: Repeating a short melodic pattern at higher or lower pitches in turn is called a:
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic idea at successively higher or lower pitches.

questions.q: A triad in 'first inversion' has which note in the bass?
questions.explain: In first inversion the third of the chord is the lowest sounding note.

questions.q: In music, what does the dynamic marking 'forte' (f) mean?
questions.explain: Forte is an Italian dynamic term meaning loud, while piano means quiet.

questions.q: What does a 'coda' provide at the end of a composition?
options: A concluding section that rounds off the piece
questions.explain: A coda is a concluding section added to round off and finish a piece of music.

questions.q: A plagal cadence (often called the 'Amen' cadence) is:
questions.explain: A plagal cadence moves from chord IV to chord I.

questions.q: Which Italian dynamic term means 'very quiet'?
questions.explain: Pianissimo (pp) means very quiet, whereas fortissimo (ff) means very loud.

questions.q: In the circle of fifths, how many sharps are in the key signature of D major?
questions.explain: D major has two sharps (F sharp and C sharp) in its key signature.

questions.q: What does the time signature 3/4 tell you?
options: Three beats in a bar, each a crotchet
Three beats in a bar, each a quaver
Four beats in a bar, each a crotchet
questions.explain: In 3/4 there are three crotchet beats per bar, giving a waltz feel.

questions.q: 'Legato' means to play notes:
questions.explain: Legato means smooth and connected, with no gaps between notes.

questions.q: A 'click track' used when recording provides:
options: A guide beat to keep performers in time
questions.explain: A click track is a steady metronome beat in the headphones that keeps performers in time while recording.

questions.q: Using repetition when developing a musical idea helps to:
options: Make ideas memorable and give a sense of unity
questions.explain: Repetition makes musical ideas memorable and gives a piece unity and coherence.

questions.q: Which composer, deaf in later life, is famous for nine symphonies and bridged the Classical and Romantic eras?
questions.explain: Beethoven wrote nine symphonies and linked the Classical and Romantic periods.

questions.q: What is 'multi-tracking' in music technology?
options: Recording parts separately and layering them together
questions.explain: Multi-tracking records different parts separately and layers them into one final mix.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, the tabla is a:
questions.explain: The tabla is a pair of hand drums providing the rhythm in Indian classical music.

questions.q: In a DAW, 'automation' is most commonly used to:
options: Make settings like volume or panning change automatically over time
questions.explain: Automation lets parameters such as volume or panning change automatically across a track over time.

questions.q: Why is tuning important before an ensemble performs?
options: So all players sound in pitch with each other
questions.explain: Tuning ensures all players' pitches match so the ensemble sounds in tune together.

questions.q: 'Quantising' in a DAW is used to:
options: Correct the timing of notes onto the beat
questions.explain: Quantising snaps recorded notes to the nearest beat to tidy up their timing.

questions.q: A DAW used for recording and sequencing music stands for:
questions.explain: DAW means Digital Audio Workstation, software used to record, edit and sequence music.
